title: Unify weight formats, sharding, and tokenizer integration to reduce cold-start and memory duplication
creator: Liam Chen
description: Background: Over several quarters we've accumulated multiple divergent model-loading code paths: legacy checkpoint loader (pickle-based), Transformers-backed pipelines, ad-hoc safetensors handling, and a worker-local tokenizer instantiation that duplicates vocab/mmap across processes. This situation increases cold-start latency, RAM usage on multi-worker nodes, and makes maintenance/error handling inconsistent. Goal: Consolidate weight format handling behind a stable compatibility layer, adopt a single preferred on-disk representation where possible (safetensors + lightweight manifest), standardize a deterministic sharding manifest and loader, and refactor tokenizer integration to a shared, lazy-loaded service within the runtime.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Single public loader API that accepts: .safetensors bundles, legacy checkpoints via compatibility shim, and quantized shards; 2) Deterministic sharding manifest format documented and used by loader; 3) Tokenizer is initialized lazily and shared between worker threads on the same host (no per-process duplicate copies); 4) Cold-start median p95 token-gen latency reduced >= 30% on baseline models; 5) End-to-end unit/integration tests cover each format and sharding scenario; 6) Migration doc and compatibility notes for ops teams.
work_items: Design compatibility shim for legacy checkpoints
Define sharding manifest schema and on-disk conventions
Implement unified loader API and registry
Refactor tokenizer initialization to shared host-level singleton
Upgrade safetensors and transformers deps with smoke tests
Roll out canary to staging and monitor metrics
risks_and_tradeoffs: Keeping backward compatibility increases surface area for bugs vs. dropping legacy support; we chose to support legacy via a shim to reduce migration friction
Shared tokenizer reduces memory but adds coordination complexity during upgrades; will gate behind runtime flag initially
Standardizing on safetensors improves safety/perf but requires conversion tooling for some customer checkpoints
